subject: parameter constraing depending on another parameter.. can we break this loop?

messages.author: 7a97c986864bf6d6
messages.subject: parameter constraing depending on another parameter.. can we break this loop?
parts:
Hello Community,

with Bob already touched this topic (https://groups.google.com/forum/#!category-topic/stan-users/general/j0VatTL7U2Q) this is an extension on that (on a simpler model).

----------------REGRESSION MODEL---y - (a * x + 0) -----------
data{
  int N;
  vector[N] y;
  real mu;
  real sigma;
  vector<lower=0>[N] x_mu;
  vector<lower=0>[N] x_sigma;
}
parameters{
  real<lower=0, upper=1> a;
  vector<lower=0>[N] x_real;
}
transformed parameters{
real<lower=0, upper=min(y ./ x_real)> a_safe;
a_safe = a;
}
model{
x_real ~ lognormal(x_mu, x_sigma);
target += lognormal_lpdf(y - (a_safe * x_real) | mu,sigma); 
}

The following numerical problems occured the indicated number of times after warmup on chain 1
                                                                                                count
validate transformed params: a_safe is 1, but must be less than or equal to 0                       2
validate transformed params: a_safe is 0.241683, but must be less than or equal to 3.74619e-08      1
validate transformed params: a_safe is 0.462863, but must be less than or equal to 0.462853         1
...
--------------POSSIBLE SOLUTION--------------------------------


Basically lognormal requires "y" > 0  --> lognormal_lpdf( y | mu, sigma);

as explained by Bob I could fix

real<lower=0, upper=min(y ./ x_real)> a;

The problem that x_real is not fixed

so I created a transformed parameter with that boundary

real<lower=0, upper=min(y ./ x_real)> a_safe;

But is obviously enough

Thanks!

messages.subject: Re: parameter constraing depending on another parameter.. can we break this loop?
parts:
I thought that because

log(mu + a*x) =  log(mu) + log(1 + (a * x)/mu)

one solution could be moving parameter to the right of the equation

target += lognormal_lpdf(y | log(mu) + log(1 + (a * x)/mu),sigma); 

OR

log(y) ~ normal(log(mu) + log(1 + (a * x)/mu), sigma);

But I miss the jacobian transformation of log(mu + a*x)

where the only parameter is "a"

Some tip on how to compensate for jacobian?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] parameter constraing depending on another parameter.. can we break this loop?
parts:
If you map a -> log(mu + a * x), and mu is not a parameter (?)
then the log Jacobian you need is just

log abs(d/d.a log(mu + a * x))

We try to follow Gelman's convention that Greek letters are parameters
and Roman letters are data, so having a data variable mu is confusing.
If in fact, you are really mapping (a, mu) -> (log(mu + a * x), mu)
where mu is a parameter, that's a different Jacobian.

- Bob
